title: Differentials of a separably generated field extension: dimension equals transcendence degree
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is finitely generated ($K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_i\in K$) and separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Let $x_1,\dots,x_r\in K$ be a transcendence basis of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] such that $K$ is separable algebraic over $k(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] (one exists, $K$ being separably generated over $k$ by the definition). Let $\Omega_{K/k}$, $\mathrm d$ be the module of Kähler differentials and the universal derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_r$ is a basis of the $K$-vector space $\Omega_{K/k}$. In particular $\Omega_{K/k}$ is finite dimensional and $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}=\operatorname{trdeg}_k(K)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree].

proof.text: Put $F=k(x_1,\dots,x_r)\subseteq K$. By [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], the $x_i$ are algebraically independent over $k$, so evaluation gives an injection $P=k[X_1,\dots,X_r]\hookrightarrow K$. Its fraction field maps isomorphically onto $F$: the image consists of the fractions $g(x)/h(x)$ with $g,h\in P$, $h\ne0$, and is precisely the smallest subfield of $K$ containing $k$ and all $x_i$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031W (lemma-derivative-zero-pth-power), lines 44189-44197, where the purely transcendental field k(x_1,...,x_r) is introduced; the fraction-field identification is expanded from Definition Tag 030E (definition-transcendence) in literature/stacks-project/fields.tex

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] (Algebra, Tag 00RX), $\Omega_{P/k}$ is free over $P$ on $\mathrm dX_1,\dots,\mathrm dX_r$. Let $S=P\setminus\{0\}$. The localization is $S^{-1}P=F$ by step 1, and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] (Algebra, Tag 00RT) gives $\Omega_{F/k}\cong S^{-1}\Omega_{P/k}$. Localizing the displayed free basis gives the $F$-basis $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_r$ of $\Omega_{F/k}$, since the localization map sends $\mathrm dX_i$ to $\mathrm dx_i$.

proof.text: The hypothesis says that $K/F$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. It is finite: if $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ as in the statement, then $K=F(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, and adjoining each algebraic $a_i$ has finite degree over the preceding field; multiplying these finitely many degrees gives $[K:F]<\infty$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-differentials-base-change] applies and makes the canonical $K$-linear map $K\otimes_F\Omega_{F/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{K/k}$, $a\otimes\mathrm df\mapsto a\,\mathrm df$, an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 031W (lemma-derivative-zero-pth-power), lines 44189-44202: K is finite separable over k(x_1,...,x_r), and the differential computation is omitted; Lemma Tag 090W (lemma-characterize-separable-algebraic-field-extensions), lines 44137-44160

proof.text: Tensoring the free $F$-module from step 2 with $K$ gives a free $K$-module with basis $1\otimes\mathrm dx_1,\dots,1\otimes\mathrm dx_r$. The isomorphism of step 3 sends these vectors to $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_r$ in $\Omega_{K/k}$, so they form a $K$-basis. It has $r$ elements; by [def-kun-transcendence-degree], a transcendence basis of $K/k$ has cardinality $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K$. Consequently $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}=r=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K$, including $r=0$.
